then.text: The tales were told, the supper was eaten, and nobody's paid for the wine. Like the old days.

else.text: Still waiting on a tale or two. The Knight and the Miller are on the Pilgrims' Way in the Kent Downs; the Wife of Bath's in the precincts, the Pardoner's by the Westgate, the Nun's Priest is down by the river.

then.text: Five tales heard, five pilgrims beaten, and every one of them thinks they won. That's a proper contest.
Chaucer's Host promised a free supper to the best teller. You heard them all and beat them all: the supper's yours, and something for the road.

else.text: {greeting} I'm Harry, the Host. Pilgrims stop here on the way to the cathedral, same as they have since Chaucer's day.
In the Tales, the Host of the Tabard in Southwark sets a contest: each pilgrim tells stories on the road, and the best wins a free supper on the way home.
I've got five pilgrims in town with tales to tell, and none of them will shut up. Go and hear them, and if they want a scrap after, give them one. Then come back and tell me who won.

quizmaster.text: Pilgrims' quiz! Five questions on the islands. No relics allowed as prizes.

ch_pilgrim.text: Walked from Southwark. Four days. My feet have their own pilgrimage now, to a bucket of hot water.
